items.headline: 'We Don't Have Decades': Why $500 Million Won't Break China's Grip on Batteries
items.snippet: Albemarle trades at $129.57 as of the September 8 close, up 60.13% over the past year but down 7.94% year to date. The stock sits in the middle of a policy story it cannot control, so the honest question is whether $500 million in federal money moves the needle for shareholders.

items.headline: Market Chatter: Lithium Miners' Profits Surge as Battery Storage Demand Drives Prices Higher
items.snippet: Lithium producers from China to Australia has seen profits soar as unrelenting demand from the energy storage sector pushes prices higher. US-headquartered Albemarle (ALB) noted that global lithium demand grew 45% through May this year, significantly outstripping supply.

items.headline: Albemarle's Lithium Math Turns Brutal
items.snippet: JPMorgan now expects lithium prices to remain in the low-$20-per-kilogram range. Albemarle faces delays at the Greenbushes CGP3 plant following a June fire. Albemarle shares were down 5.16% at $134.21 at the time of publication on Tuesday.

items.headline: Albemarle price target lowered to $225 from $245 at Truist
items.snippet: Truist analyst Peter Osterland lowered the firm's price target on Albemarle to $225 from $245 and keeps a Buy rating on the shares, citing resilient lithium demand and constrained supply dynamics.
